Summarize fitted Gaussian smoothing scales

Source: R/gaussian_scale_conductance.R
gaussian_scale_summary.Rd

Converts fitted Gaussian sigma parameters into map-unit, cell-based, and Gaussian-kernel interpretation summaries for a fitted model produced with gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance.

Usage

gaussian_scale_summary(
  object,
  probabilities = c(0.5, 0.95),
  distance_per_map_unit = NULL,
  distance_unit = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted terradish object using the Gaussian scale-aware conductance model.

probabilities

Probabilities used to summarize the one-dimensional half-width and two-dimensional radial extent of the Gaussian kernel.

distance_per_map_unit

Optional scalar conversion factor used to express sigma and the derived radii in user-supplied distance units. For example, if the raster CRS is in meters, use distance_per_map_unit = 0.001 and distance_unit = "km" to report kilometers.

distance_unit

Optional label used when distance_per_map_unit is supplied.

Value

A data frame with one row per fitted sigma parameter. covariate identifies the layer. sigma is its fitted map-unit scale; sigma_lower and sigma_upper are fitting bounds. sigma_internal, sigma_conversion, and sigma_conversion_mode describe the optimization units. native_unit labels map units or degrees, and sigma_cells_x, sigma_cells_y express the scale in cell widths. Probability-specific axis_* and radial_* columns give the theoretical Gaussian distances described above, in native units and, when requested, converted units. They describe the untruncated Gaussian; retained raster windows can omit some of that mass.

Details

The returned table always reports sigma on the raster's native map scale and in raster cell widths. When sigma conversion is enabled during fitting, the table also reports the internal optimization scale and its conversion factor back to map units. For each probability p, axis_* gives the one-dimensional half-width \(\sigma \Phi^{-1}((1+p)/2)\), while radial_* gives the isotropic two-dimensional radius \(\sigma\sqrt{-2\log(1-p)}\) containing proportion p of the Gaussian kernel mass. Here \(\Phi^{-1}\) is the standard normal quantile function and \(\sigma\) is the smoothing scale. These quantities summarize the fitted raster-smoothing kernel. They are not estimates of dispersal distance, movement distance, or home-range size. Use summary(object)$sigma_table to inspect standard errors and bound flags, and confint(object) for bound-truncated intervals; smoothing scales have no reported z or p values. Use gaussian_scale_profile when a profile interval is needed. A positive scale can reflect dispersal averaging, and even the half-cell lower bound applies some smoothing.

If the retained raster is in longitude/latitude, the native-unit results are in degrees. In that case, use a projected raster for direct distance interpretation, or provide an approximate distance_per_map_unit conversion if you need a quick descriptive summary. Without a conversion the function warns once per session, and the native_unit column reads "degrees" on every call.

See also

gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance, gaussian_scale_profile, plot.terradish

Other spatial scale: gaussian_scale_profile(), gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(), terradish_scale_optim()

Examples

# \donttest{
data(melip)
forestcover <- terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover)
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(forestcover) <- "forestcover"

# Coarsen the raster so the example runs quickly; the Gaussian model
# re-smooths the layer at every optimizer step, so cost scales with cell
# count. Use the full resolution in a real analysis.
forestcover <- terra::aggregate(forestcover, fact = 3, na.rm = TRUE)

# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(forestcover, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]

# Feed the model the raw (unsmoothed, unstandardized) raster: it smooths and
# standardizes internally at each candidate sigma.
surface <- conductance_surface(forestcover, coords[keep], saveStack = TRUE)
fit <- terradish(Fst ~ forestcover,
                 data = surface,
                 conductance_model =
                   gaussian_smoothed_loglinear_conductance(surface),
                 measurement_model = leastsquares,
                 optimizer = "bfgs")

# sigma is in map units. The melip rasters are unprojected, so those units
# are degrees; distance_per_map_unit rescales the reported distances
# (roughly 111 km per degree near the equator). Without a conversion the
# function warns that the scale is in degrees.
scales <- gaussian_scale_summary(fit, distance_per_map_unit = 111,
                                 distance_unit = "km")
scales
#>     covariate     sigma sigma_lower sigma_upper sigma_internal sigma_conversion
#> 1 forestcover 0.2621598      0.0675        1.17       1.941924            0.135
#>   sigma_conversion_mode native_unit sigma_cells_x sigma_cells_y   axis_50
#> 1                  cell     degrees      1.941924      1.941924 0.1768241
#>   radial_50   axis_95 radial_95 sigma_km sigma_lower_km sigma_upper_km
#> 1 0.3086696 0.5138238 0.6417008 29.09974         7.4925         129.87
#>   axis_50_km radial_50_km axis_95_km radial_95_km
#> 1   19.62748     34.26232   57.03444     71.22879
# One row per smoothed layer: sigma, its bounds, and the kernel radii.
scales[, c("covariate", "sigma", "sigma_lower", "sigma_upper")]
#>     covariate     sigma sigma_lower sigma_upper
#> 1 forestcover 0.2621598      0.0675        1.17
# }
